title: Cline MCP: Setup Guide for MCP Servers (2026)
summary: Cline MCP is the tool-connection layer for Cline, an open-source AI coding agent. Configure it free and avoid common setup mistakes.
body_markdown:
## Stage 2: Add your first MCP server and run a tool


Open the MCP Servers panel in Cline, install one server from the marketplace or add it by hand in cline_mcp_settings.json, and wait for a green status before running any tool.


### Install an MCP server from the Cline marketplace


Pick the marketplace tab in the MCP Servers panel, find a server, and press Install. Cline fetches it and writes the entry into your settings file for you.


For a first server, choose something read-only or low-stakes. A wrong tool call against a notes folder costs you a retry. A wrong call against a live ticketing system costs you an apology email.


Use the panel's option to configure MCP servers, and Cline opens cline_mcp_settings.json. Each server is an entry under` mcpServers` with a` command` , its` args` , and optionally an` env` block for secrets such as API tokens.


> A wrong tool call against a notes folder costs you a retry. A wrong call against a live ticketing system costs you an apology email.


```text
{
"mcpServers": {
"notes": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/home/me/notes"]
}
}
}
```


Keep tokens in` env` , not in` args` , so they stay out of the command line you paste into chat or a ticket.


### Local stdio versus remote servers


When Cline starts a program on your machine and talks to it through standard input and output, that is a local stdio server. That's what the` command` and` args` entry above does.


Whatever it can touch, your machine can touch, so the folder or account you hand it is your real exposure.


Point Cline at a URL instead of a command and you have a remote server, one that runs elsewhere. You trust the operator's handling of your data, and your settings carry whatever credentials it requires.


Activepieces is one such remote server, with a per-project MCP server whose tools are the very same integration actions that run as steps in its flows.


Each integration is defined once in packages/pieces of the open source repo, which holds 750 integrations under an MIT-licensed core, and the Integrations Framework and MCP Server docs describe how that one definition serves both uses.


Connect an integration once and it is both a flow step and a tool, so there is no second integration to build for your agent. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


### Run a first tool call and read the approval prompt


Look at the server's status dot first. Green means Cline connected and listed its tools. Anything else means the tool will fail, so fix the command or credentials before blaming the model.


Then ask Cline for something that needs the server, such as listing the files in the notes folder. Cline pauses and shows which server and tool it wants to call, with the arguments.


Read the arguments, not just the tool name. Approving a "write" call with the wrong path is the mistake you can't undo.


Leave auto-approve off for now. Turn it on per tool only after you've watched that tool behave correctly.
